description:
Lintu takımı, lise yıllarında başlayan sağlam bir arkadaşlığın ve ortak bir geleceği inşa etme tutkusunun ürünü. Yerli ve milli teknoloji hamlesinden aldığımız ilham ve sarsılmaz çalışma azmiyle, Türkiye’nin gelişen yapay zeka serüveninde sadece izleyici kalmayı reddediyoruz. Temellerimizi bu topraklara atarken, gözümüzü ve hedefimizi sınırların ötesine dikiyoruz.

Hackathonlarda ve geliştirdiğimiz ana projelerde ürettiğimiz özgün fikirlerle, küresel ölçekte rekabet edebilen uluslararası bir teknoloji takımı olmayı amaçlıyoruz. Sektör liderleriyle sınırları aşan iş birlikleri kurarak, yalnızca çağa yetişmeyi değil; yerli zekamızı küresel pazarda temsil edip yapay zeka dünyasında geleceğe yön veren çözümlere imza atmayı hedefliyoruz.
summary: We built the Fire Activity Calendar, a free web app that turns 26 years of NASA FIRMS fire detections (MODIS 2000–2026 and VIIRS 2012–2026) into one consistent calendar and map. When the sharper VIIRS sensor joined in 2012, raw fire counts over Türkiye jumped by 143%, although MODIS alone fell by 45% over the same period. We solve this in two steps. First, we cluster detections from both satellites into single fire events: 1.04 million clean detections become 471,978 events, avoiding 59,201 double counts. Second, we translate VIIRS into a "MODIS-equivalent" series learned per region, season and fire power. A leave-one-year-out test gives a yearly error of 8.3% (R² 0.87). To show the method is not tuned to one country, we ran the same pipeline on the USA (2009–2015): a fake +319% jump becomes −4.8%, against −2.1% for real MODIS, and 32 of 33 documented large fires match a satellite event. The app works offline and on phones, with a Türkiye | USA switch. This matters because MODIS retires in 2027: our bridge lets VIIRS continue a comparable fire record, so long-term fire trends stay meaningful.
details:
Live app: https://lintuteam.github.io/lintu-fireatlas/
Source code: https://github.com/Lintuteam/lintu-fireatlas
USA validation view: https://lintuteam.github.io/lintu-fireatlas/arayuz/abd.html

What it does. The app shows when and where Türkiye burned from 2000 to today. A calendar matrix (years × months) shows fire events per month. A star marks each year's busiest month and a flame marks the month of that year's largest fire. Clicking a month opens its fires on an interactive map. The map shows a density heat map when zoomed out and single fire events when zoomed in. Users can select a province, a circle or a polygon, hide field (stubble) burning, list the ten most powerful fires, and play a "2012 jump mode" that shows the same map in three stages: raw, clustered and corrected. A Türkiye | USA switch in the header opens the same analysis for the USA, and the layout adapts to phones (the filter panel folds into one button).

How it works.

  1. Raw data: 1,414,674 NASA FIRMS detections over Türkiye (MODIS C6.1: 259,707; VIIRS 375 m: 1,154,967).
  2. Cleaning: every detection gets one label, and nothing is deleted. Labels: clean fire, stubble burning, static/industrial heat source, offshore, volcano, persistent-uncertain. The rules are transparent, not a black-box model.
  3. Clustering: detections that are close in space and time are linked in a graph, using both satellites together. Each connected component is one fire event. This cuts the 2012 jump from +143% to +31%.
  4. Harmonization: VIIRS counts are first divided by the number of satellites flying (effort correction), then scaled by a region × season × fire-power ratio learned from the years when both sensors overlap. Leave-one-year-out validation over 2012–2025: yearly MAPE 8.3%, R² 0.87. The monthly national uncertainty band covers real MODIS 92% of the time.

Validation.

  • The final activity map highlights the same regions as the Türkiye wildfire risk map published by TRT Haber.
  • With no official data in the model, our largest event is the 2021 Manavgat fire: 6,740 detections, about 218 hours, matching the official dates of 28 July – 6 August 2021.
  • 16 of our 20 largest events match documented wildfires, 3 match partly, and 1 was not found.
  • Second country: we ran the same pipeline on NASA FIRMS data for the USA (2009–2015, 2.72 million detections). The raw 2012 jump of +319% becomes −4.8% in our MODIS-equivalent series, against −2.1% for real MODIS (2.7 points apart; yearly leave-one-year-out error 4.2%). 32 of 33 documented large US wildfires match a satellite event, and an independent re-computation reproduced the counts, jumps and test errors exactly.

Accessibility. All palettes are colour-blind safe (Viridis/Cividis), with a one-click protan/deutan/tritan simulation. The app runs in Turkish and English, works fully offline, and includes Lintu, a 14-step guided tour. On phones the layout switches to a single column.

Honest limits.

  • This is a record of past fire activity, not a fire-risk forecast.
  • 2026 is a partial, near-real-time year, and Aqua's orbit drift lowers confidence in its correction.
  • Stubble and industrial labels are rule-based estimates.
  • Recall for small fires was not measured.

Benefits and goals. MODIS retires in 2027. Our method keeps a comparable 26-year record alive with VIIRS. The same pipeline runs on FIRMS data for any country. We have already tested it on the USA (see Validation). The app is free and offline, so researchers, journalists and forest services can use it without special software.

Tools. Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy) for the data pipeline and validation; plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet for the offline web app; Matplotlib for figures; PowerPoint for the demo deck.
